question: Which of the following peptides are not produced by the renal system?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Renin" -> "produced by juxtaglomerular cells in kidneys" -> "part of renal system" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Angiotensin I" -> "produced by conversion of angiotensinogen by renin" -> "occurs in bloodstream" -> "not directly produced by renal system" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Erythropoietin" -> "produced by interstitial fibroblasts in kidneys" -> "part of renal system" -> 90%
CHAIN: "1,25DHCC" -> "active form of vitamin D" -> "converted in kidneys" -> "produced by renal system" -> 90%
analysis: The question asks which peptide is not produced by the renal system. Renin is produced by the juxtaglomerular cells in the kidneys, and erythropoietin is produced by interstitial fibroblasts in the kidneys, both clearly part of the renal system. 1,25-Dihydroxycholecalciferol (1,25DHCC) is the active form of vitamin D, converted in the kidneys, thus also associated with the renal system. Angiotensin I, however, is formed in the bloodstream when renin acts on angiotensinogen, which is produced by the liver. Therefore, Angiotensin I is not directly produced by the renal system. This aligns with standard medical knowledge and consensus.
